2. Short fact, necessary for the purpose of this Rule, is that the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 before the Assistant Judge, Galachipa, Patuakhali impleading the opposite parties as defendants seeking a decree for declaration of their title in the suit land stating, inter alia, that the land appertaining to CS Khatian Nos. 17, 217, 218, of Mouja Chhailabunia of Police-Station-Galachipa originally belonged to Araj Ali to the extent of one-third share, who having been in possession and enjoyment thereof died leaving behind one son the plaintiffs No.1 and two daughters Aziful Bibi, Karful Bibi, and a wife Meherjan as his heirs; Karful Bibi died unmarried leaving behind her mother Meherjan, brother the plaintiff No.1 and a sister Aziful Bibi the plaintiff No. 2. Thereafter, Meherjan died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos.1 and 2 as her sole heirs; it is also, stated by the plaintiffs that during SA operation plaintiffs' share was wrongly recorded as 2 annas 13 gandas I Kara and I Karanti. Though as a matter of fact the remaining 2 annas 13 gondas I Kara I Karanti share was wrongly recorded in favour of some of the defendants as also in favour of the predecessors of some others, who have no right, title, interest or possession therein; it was further stated in the plaint that on 13-5-1985 when the defendants attempted to invade the right of the plaintiffs over the suit land on the basis of such erroneous record of right the plaintiffs brought the suit claiming their title in the suit land which has been in their possession, as stated above. 

 3. The defendant No. 4 entered appearance upon filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land appertaining to CS Khatian Nos.17, 217, 218 and 219, rather one Alef Chowkider was the exclusive owner in possession of the said land; said Alef Chowkider married Mayajan the mother of one Sharap Ali who was the grandfather of defendant No. 4 while Araj Ali is the son of Mohammed Jan who was the former husband of Maynajan. It was further alleged in the written statement that one-third share was collusively recorded in favour of the predecessor of the plaintiffs during CS operation which was not correct; Alef Chowkikder gifted away some land to the extent of 1.52 acres in favour of Sharaf Ali by a deed of gift dated 14 Falgoon 1326 BS and had handed over possession; it was also stated in the written statement that Araj Ali also executed a nadabinama in respect of the said land in favour of Sworup Ali on 28 Chaitra, 1344 BS. Subsequently, the SA record was correctly prepared in his favour, the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land hence the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 10. Upon consideration of the aforesaid materials and submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner, particularly when he relied upon the decision given by a Division Bench of Calcutta High Court as referred to above, wherefrom I find that the said decision has got a direct bearing in the present case. More particularly, when the earlier suit, being Title Suit No. 106 of 1968, was a suit for correction of record of right disclosing a particular cause of action arose in the year 1968, while the present suit being Title Suit No. 81 of 1985 was instituted seeking a decree for simple declaration of title on the basis of a cause of action which arose on 13-5-1985 when a threat of invasion of the right of the plaintiffs was demonstrated by the defendants then only the plaintiffs took recourse to institution of the present suit. This Court being in respectful agreement with the principle of law enunciated in the case referred to above, also finds that the expression subject matter as used in Order XXIII rule I means a series of acts or transactions alleged to exist giving rise to the relief claimed. As such, the first series of facts or transactions, which formed the basis of the first suit being Title Suit No.106 of 1968 was based on erroneous record of right, in the SA Khatian and the suit was brought from the date of knowledge with respect to such wrong record of right but in the instant suit namely, Title Suit No. 81 of 1985, the date of threatened invasion over the right of the plaintiffs on 13-5-1985 was the cause of action and not the erroneous record of right, besides the relief claimed in that suit cannot be said to be one and the same. Therefore, in my opinion, the previous suit was instituted with a different subject matter than that of the present suit and that the relief claimed in that suit is not the same as in the present case besides, the cause of action in that suit is not the same as in the present one. Therefore, institution of the previous suit cannot have any bearing in instituting the present suit and in that view of the matter, the institution of the previous suit cannot be a ground for treating the present suit as one barred by limitation under Article 122 of the Limitation Act.
